newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai finance groups eye mergers, bank upgrades.
newsitem.headline: Thai finance groups eye mergers, bank upgrades.

text.p: Bank of Thailand Governor Rerngchai Marakanond said on Tuesday four to five groups of finance companies have proposed to merge in the wake of relaxed new government measures to encourage corporate alliances in the troubled sector.
"About four to five groups (of finance companies) have put in merger applications," Rerngchai told reporters.
"Some of the groups are also interested in applying for new banking licenses," Rerngchai said.
The government on Tuesday issued four urgent decrees aimed at averting a crisis in troubled finance and property sectors.

The decrees will smooth out the process for merging finance companies to transfer doubtful loan accounts, waive taxes and transaction fees arising from mergers, and authorise companies to hold extra shareholders meetings to approve corporate alliances.
Rerngchai did not identify companies planning to merge.
One group of finance firms seeking to merge earlier was made up of Nava Finance and Securities Plc, Thaimex Finance and Securities Plc, CMIC Finance and Securities Plc and Thai Thanakorn Finance Plc.
Two other groups showing interest were led by SITCA Investment and Securities Plc and Industrial Finance Corp of Thailand.
